The "who reacted to whom" debate is fun, but it kind of misses the point: a price cut is reversible, a weight release isn't. Once these weights are out, nobody can charge much above inference cost for that capability band ever again. That's a ratchet, not a news cycle.

And it's landing on the tier that actually generates the token volume. Frontier evals are marketing; the money is in the boring high-throughput stuff — classification, extraction, routing, tool-calling loops, retries — where you burn billions of tokens and never needed 5.6-level reasoning in the first place. Commoditizing the "flash" tier hurts a lot more than losing the top of a benchmark chart.

Closed labs' margin lives in the gap above the open frontier, and that gap keeps getting squeezed from below faster than it grows from above.
